race.name: GFNY Miami
race.tagline: Two fully closed-road laps on Krome Avenue: 52 fast, exposed miles where wind, positioning, and group discipline decide the race.

vitals.date: April annually (moved from November to April starting the 2027 edition)
vitals.start_format: Mass-start competitive long course with chip timing
vitals.registration: Online through the official GFNY Miami race site
vitals.feed_zones: Official GFNY aid stations with hydration, food, technical, and medical support
vitals.cutoff_time: Long-course riders must begin lap two at mile 26.3 by 8:50 a.m., equivalent to a 15 mph average
route_options: Competitive long route: 84 km / 52 mi — two laps
Recreational medium route: 42 km / 26 mi — one lap

climate.description: The April course is flat and open, making sun, humidity, and especially wind the environmental variables that shape the race. With no meaningful climbing to break the field naturally, changing wind direction and time spent sheltered in a group matter throughout both laps.
challenges: Repeated accelerations around groups and turns

terrain.primary: Flat, fully closed Krome Avenue circuit
terrain.surface: Paved state highway on a fully closed four-lane course. The technical demand comes from pack movement and wind rather than corners or descents.
features: Two 26-mile out-and-back laps for the competitive course
Average course elevation of approximately six feet above sea level
All four lanes of Krome Avenue closed to vehicles
Wide, flat roads that reward drafting and positioning
Wind is the primary obstacle rather than elevation

fondo_rating.scoring_notes: Regraded against the verified 2027 format: a short 52-mile long course limits endurance difficulty, while the fully closed four-lane highway and smooth paved surface raise organization and road-surface scores.

climb_profile.king_of_mountain: None. The official course averages approximately six feet above sea level.

course_description.character: The competitive route starts and finishes at Miccosukee Casino & Resort and covers two 26-mile out-and-back laps on Krome Avenue. All four lanes are closed, creating a rare wide-open racing surface. The course is almost perfectly flat, so wind, peloton position, and the ability to repeat accelerations matter more than climbing or descending skill.
course_description.signature_challenge: Holding position and conserving energy in exposed wind across two flat laps. Riders who lose the right group have no terrain-driven regrouping opportunity.

logistics.airport: Miami International Airport (MIA) — direct flights from major cities worldwide. Fort Lauderdale (FLL) also works, 30 minutes north.
logistics.lodging_strategy: Stay near Miccosukee Casino & Resort to simplify the early start, or farther east if combining the race with a Miami trip. Account for the long drive from the beach districts to western Miami-Dade.
logistics.transport: Use the official race-week guide for parking and access around the fully closed Krome Avenue course.
logistics.food: Miami's food scene is world-class. Cuban, Haitian, Colombian, and everything else. Post-ride fueling is not a problem.

history.origin_story: GFNY brought its competitive mass-participation format to Miami in 2024. The event uses a fully closed section of Krome Avenue west of the city, trading climbing for unusually controlled road access and wind-driven pack racing.
notable_moments: 2011: GFNY launches in New York City as a competitive gran fondo with anti-doping — unusual for the US market
2026: Third edition held on a fully closed four-lane highway
2027: Race scheduled for April 4 with a two-lap 52-mile competitive course
history.reputation: A short, exceptionally flat GFNY whose distinguishing feature is a genuinely closed-road racing environment.

biased_opinion.summary: GFNY Miami is only 52 miles, but the fully closed four-lane course gives it a race-day quality that many longer fondos cannot match. With essentially no elevation, every tactical mistake is exposed: miss the split, spend too long in the wind, or burn matches before lap two and there is nowhere to hide. It is not a destination climbing course; it is a compact, fast group-riding test.
strengths: GFNY competitive classification: anti-doping, chip timing, age-group rankings — rare in the gran fondo world
All four lanes closed to vehicles
Simple course navigation and minimal descending risk
MIA is a global hub with abundant lodging
Group-riding tactics matter from the opening miles
weaknesses: The 52-mile competitive route is short for a destination gran fondo
No meaningful climbing or descending variety
Wind can turn a missed group into a long solo effort
Western Miami-Dade start is distant from Miami's beach districts
biased_opinion.bottom_line: Race it for closed roads and fast pack dynamics. Choose another GFNY if climbing, distance, or scenery is the reason you travel.

final_verdict.one_liner: Fifty-two fully closed-road miles where wind, positioning, and group discipline replace climbing.
final_verdict.should_you_race: Yes if you value genuinely closed roads, fast pack racing, and easy destination logistics. Skip it if a long endurance challenge or meaningful climbing is essential.
final_verdict.alternatives: GFNY NYC for the flagship experience, GFNY Maryland for a longer rolling course, or GFNY Sebring for another Florida event.
